title: ‘Unbelievably savage’ dog neutralised after attacking woman and child in O'Briensbridge
excerpt: A YOUNG child and woman in her 50s have been hospitalised following an “unbelievably savage” dog attack in East Clare.
author: Michael Fitzgerald
alt: ‘Unbelievably savage’ dog neutralised after attacking woman and child in O'Briensbridge
body: A YOUNG child and woman in her 50s have been hospitalised following an “unbelievably savage” dog attack in East Clare.

In a statement to The Clare Echo, Gardaí confirmed that they and “emergency services responded to an incident involving a dog at O’Briensbridge, Co. Clare, on Saturday 8th August 2026, that occurred at approximately 10.55am”.

“A woman (aged in her 50’s) received injuries believed to be non-life-threatening at this time. The services of the Dog Warden were requested. Attempts were made to sedate the animal who had to be neutralised and removed from the scene by the Dog Warden”, they continued. Gardaí went on to state that no further information in relation to the incident is available at this time and that investigations into the attack are ongoing.

The Clare Echo understands that the sheepdog had been chained up before escaping and attacking the woman as well as the young boy. The dog also attacked members of An Garda Siochána before being brought under control.

Appearing on RTÉ’s News at One programme, Clare County Council Chief Dog Warden Frankie Coote stated that “I’m not exaggerating to say that I honestly believe if we hadn’t removed him on the day, he was capable of actually killing an older person or a child. He was an unbelievably more savage dog than I had seen in any breed”.

“I’d like to stress here that 99% of sheepdogs, they’re trained and they’re working, you know, and the worst you might get off them is a bite on the ankle as you run away, or they chase a bike. This was exceptional circumstances. A terrible scene to see, I haven’t seen anything like that before, where you come and a dog is a danger. But it’s removed now and it’s gone”, Coote continued.

The dog warden emphasised on the programme that any dog is capable of attack, adding that the young boy was released from hospital that evening with “a few stitches”, while the injuries received by the woman were more serious.

title: 'There was acceptance to Ardnacrusha, now there's signs around here saying no wind turbines'
excerpt: Oonagh Buckley, Secretary General of the Department of Climate, Energy and the Environment; Terence O’Rourke, Chairman of ESB; Paddy Hayes, CEO of ESB; Minister for Climate, Energy and Environment Darragh O’Brien; and Bevin Cody, ESB Networks, pictured at an EU Presidency event at Ardnacrusha hydroelectric power station
author: Páraic McMahon
alt: 'There was acceptance to Ardnacrusha, now there's signs around here saying no wind turbines'
body: Oonagh Buckley, Secretary General of the Department of Climate, Energy and the Environment; Terence O’Rourke, Chairman of ESB; Paddy Hayes, CEO of ESB; Minister for Climate, Energy and Environment Darragh O’Brien; and Bevin Cody, ESB Networks, pictured at an EU Presidency event at Ardnacrusha hydroelectric power station

PEOPLE must see benefits to their local area in order to support major infrastructural projects, the CEO of EirGrid has told a conference in South-East Clare with the Secretary General of the Department of Environment referencing signs in the county objecting to wind turbines.
To kick off Ireland’s Presidency of the Council of the European Union, energy priorities for the State within the historic turbine hall of Ardnacrusha Power Station.

Secretary General at the Department of Climate, Energy and Environment, Oonagh Buckley moderated a panel discussion titled ‘Electrified energy systems: Innovation powering our grid; A resilient, fair, affordable energy system’.

A native of Cork City, Oonagh’s grandfathers, Timothy Buckley and Tomás Ryle both engineers were involved in the construction of the Shannon Scheme from October 1925 until July 1929. Timothy a civil engineer from Cork worked on the road and ramps while Kerry native Tomás an electrical engineer worked on the generators, ironically both men never met while working as sub-contractors for Siemens Schukert.

She revealed her connections during the beginning of the conference, “to be a young man working here would have been incredibly exciting”. She said any infrastructural project in the modern world “is “really important that we design it right and that it works for every country in the world”.

Founder and Executive Chair of Trifecta Energy CLG, Lesley O’Connor referred to Ireland being a wealthy country yet one which experiences fuel poverty, “households experience a choice between food and fuel”. She stated, “We need to be clear on where we are today, our electricity prices are among the highest in Europe which is two to three times higher than Asia and the USA. We have to lean into the affordability thing, energy is really complex, there is no silver bullet, everyone wants one but it doesn’t exist. We need to be clear, up front, honest and transparent to our public, we have a pathway but we build a system. We’re not going to solve everything tomorrow”.

CEO of EirGrid, Cathal Marlay outlined, “our grid has to completely transform which is a massive challenge. It requires big investment which is a big challenge”. Scaling up is essential but requires working closely and communicating with customers.

Signs across South-East Clare objecting to wind turbines were referenced by the Secretary General. “There was acceptance to Ardnacrusha and people saw the good it would bring.. You all passed on your way here signs up saying no wind turbines, it is a very different narrative on electrification. We are now seeing a very strong pushback against slogans or previous pitches, net zero is now a political culture war and a real problem”.

Responding to this, Marley commented, “All politics is local, what people need to see and one of the biggest challenges is big infrastructure and their impact on landscape, the national broadband impact was evident quickly and people loved, people saw straight away the benefits”.

Referencing another contentious plan affecting the people of Clare, namely the 170km pipeline from the River Shannon to Dublin, he stated, “there are no benefits in their own area like bringing the water from the Shannon to Dublin”. He stressed, “for the biggest projects you have to give benefits to the local areas, people ask why are we putting this infrastructure in our landscape if we’re not seeing impact”. He maintained success will be achieved by demonstrating local benefits and a national campaign.

Other panellists voiced the need for people to see an impact in their pockets which will lead them to question if it makes sense and deliver savings while also providing local employment opportunities.

Jane Cohen of the International Energy Agency (IEA) outlined, “This is at the heart of how we move this forward”. She said, “All of the work we’re doing is about people’s lives, if they don’t feel it or if it is lost in technical jargon then it won’t move forward. It needs to be more than a news slogan, it is hard to scale, it is like it is a side project rather than the basis of the programme”.

title: 'Too much stuff is online' – West Clare councillors look for greater public accessibility for meetings
excerpt: WEST Clare councillors have called for Municipal District meetings to be brought into local communities as part of efforts to make local government more accessible.
author: Paige Foley
alt: 'Too much stuff is online' – West Clare councillors look for greater public accessibility for meetings
body: WEST Clare councillors have called for Municipal District meetings to be brought into local communities as part of efforts to make local government more accessible.
The proposal emerged during a discussion at the July meeting of the West Clare Municipal District, where councillors debated new ways of engaging with residents and young people.

Cllr Joe Garrihy (FG) said local authorities continued to grapple with how to encourage people to become involved in local decision-making. He suggested the Municipal District consider holding meetings in community halls across West Clare, including areas such as Corofin and Liscannor.
“Too much stuff is online,” he said, arguing that taking meetings into communities would help tackle misinformation and make local government more accessible.

Cllr Gabriel Keating (FG) recalled previous visits by primary and secondary school students to council meetings, describing them as a “fantastic” way of engaging young people before they were disrupted by the Covid-19 pandemic.

Senior Executive Officer John O'Malley said the council's Town Centre First programme had demonstrated how engaged young people could be when given the opportunity to participate and suggested the existing Town Team structure could help support future engagement.
He also asked whether councillors wanted to explore holding future Municipal District meetings in other locations across West Clare, telling members the proposal would be investigated.

Cllr Shane Talty (FF) suggested councillors engage with secondary schools in North and West Clare over the next 12 months to assess whether they would be interested in hosting council meetings, saying a school hall could provide an opportunity to involve dozens of students.
Cathaoirleach Cllr Michael Shannon (FF) backed the proposal, saying councillors needed to connect more with young people and local communities.

He also pointed to practical benefits of rotating meeting venues and potentially inviting community groups and residents to attend the next municipal district meeting in Kilrush in September as the council begins to explore the idea.
Director of Service Carmel Kirby said community engagement should extend beyond schools and include other groups with an interest in local issues.

Concluding the discussion, Cllr Ian Lynch (IND) said previous meetings held in schools had shown that young people were more likely to engage if discussions focused on issues relevant to them, rather than sitting through a full council meeting.

He also supported bringing meetings into communities but said residents needed to know in advance when meetings were taking place and be given opportunities to participate. “If we're going into the community, have a meeting for the community,” he said, suggesting local groups such as Tidy Towns should be invited to take part.
No formal decision was taken, but councillors agreed the proposal was worth exploring.

title: Clooney Quin's firepower lays foundation for victory
excerpt: HAVING failed to score a goal in their opening round draw with Cratloe, Clooney/Quin bagged 4-11 in the first half of their dominant victory over Feakle.
author: Gearóid Howley
alt: Clooney Quin's firepower lays foundation for victory
body: HAVING failed to score a goal in their opening round draw with Cratloe, Clooney/Quin bagged 4-11 in the first half of their dominant victory over Feakle.

Manager Fergal Lynch felt the foundations for their win were laid in that opening half by which they held a sixteen point advantage.“We had a great start, we had a strong breeze in the first half and we capitalised on that. Feakle then, they were coming into play with a really good breeze in the second half, but I suppose the damage was done for us in the first half,” he said.

After keeping a clean sheet and grabbing four green flags themselves, Lynch felt the 4-17 to 0-13 victory was a much more complete performance than their share of the spoils against Cratloe a fortnight ago.

He told The Clare Echo, “We conceded a goal the last day in the first round against Cratloe and we didn’t have any goal threat at all. That was something we had addressed and we had worked on during the last two weeks, so thankfully that has come off. Cratloe had five goal chances the last day and we had a plus one that day and we were disappointed with it, so we rectified that and thankfully we came through”.

Last year’s beaten county finalists got a return of 4-10 from their starting front-six with late changes Darragh McNamara and Jerry O’Connor scoring 2-0 and 1-2 respectively. “Peter [Duggan], and Jack [O’Neill], and Jerry [O’Connor] had a great impetus in the half-forward line, we just made a few changes there. We brought in Darragh McNamara after a long layoff with his hips since the county final last year so it’s great that they’re getting game time and the lads are playing with a little bit of freedom and a smile on their face”.

Heading into their final group-stage game against O’Callaghan’s Mills, Clooney/Quin sit at the top of Group 3 unbeaten on three points. However, their fate is yet to be decided, with Cratloe, Feakle, and the aforementioned O’Callaghan’s Mills all still in with a chance of qualifying for the knockout stages.

“As I said to the players there, this is very similar to what happened us last year, we’d a very poor performance against Broadford, came through by the skin of our teeth, performed really well against Inagh/Kilnamona and then not so well against Corofin in the third round. This is step two of six steps and we’re going to get ourselves ready for the Mills in step three and whatever happens after that happens,” he concluded.

title: Lissycasey & Kilmurry Ibrickane a 'winner takes all' tie
excerpt: LISSYCASEY are treating Friday’s second round showdown with Kilmurry Ibrickane as “winner takes all”.
author: Páraic McMahon
alt: Lissycasey & Kilmurry Ibrickane a 'winner takes all' tie
body: LISSYCASEY are treating Friday’s second round showdown with Kilmurry Ibrickane as “winner takes all”.
Both sides prevailed in their first round encounters in Group 3 of the TUS Clare SFC meaning the victor this weekend is guaranteed of a place in the knockout stages.
Automatic qualification to the Cusack Cup final was secured by Lissycasey when they defeated Kilmurry Ibrickane 4-21 3-6 in the last round of the league.

Speaking to The Clare Echo, Lissycasey manager David Considine said the league tie will count for nothing this weekend while praising the manner of Kilmurry Ibrickane’s first round showing over St Breckans. “They were very impressive, they are a quality team, we played them in the last group stage of the Cusack Cup in the seventh round, the scoreline was what it was but we said straight away after that game that we will be playing them in round two of the championship and they will have different players out on the field, they are a championship team”.

Heaping praise on the Bricks, Considine stated, “they have the pedigree, they have lads in the squad that have won multiple Jack Daly medals, we’re well aware that we will be very much up against it, we will be underdogs going in against Kilmurry Ibrickane, both teams have got two points on the board so it is a winner take all in the sense that the winners puts themselves in a very strong position and whoever loses is back to the status quo and will be joined by someone else on two points potentially, it will be all to play for going into round three if the result isn’t positive”.

title: Minor glory for Newmarket-on-Fergus & Doora/Barefield
excerpt: NEWMARKET-ON-Fergus claimed a second Minor A camogie championship in three years when defeating Sixmilebridge.
author: Páraic McMahon
alt: Minor glory for Newmarket-on-Fergus & Doora/Barefield
body: NEWMARKET-ON-Fergus claimed a second Minor A camogie championship in three years when defeating Sixmilebridge.
In a dominant display, the Blues overcame their neigbhours on a score of 2-18 1-4.
Aoibhe O’Leary who forms part of the Newmarket-on-Fergus senior side accounted for eight points in the opening half to help her side to a 0-11 0-3 cushion by the half-time whistle.
Victory was secured for Newmarket-on-Fergus in the second half with Darcey Ryan and Hollie Earls striking for goals in the third quarter of the contest.

St Joseph's Doora/Barefield reigned supreme in the Minor B camogie final with a 1-16 1-9 victory over Whitegate. The Parish produced a strong second half where they outscored their East Clare opponents 1-8 0-4 with Lauren Shannon raising the green flag. The sides were tied at half time and had been level on five occasions in the opening half.

title: Businesses losing 'thousands of euro' amid Ennistymon public realm delays
excerpt: FRUSTRATION is mounting over delays to the Ennistymon public realm project, with councillors warning that businesses are losing thousands of euro during the height of the tourism season.
author: Paige Foley
alt: Businesses losing 'thousands of euro' amid Ennistymon public realm delays
body: FRUSTRATION is mounting over delays to the Ennistymon public realm project, with councillors warning that businesses are losing thousands of euro during the height of the tourism season.

The issue was raised under at the July meeting of the West Clare Municipal District, where Cllr Bill Slattery (FG) said while people welcomed the public realm project, there was growing anger over the length of time the works were taking to complete.
He said local businesses, particularly restaurants, had lost “thousands of euros” in footfall as a result of the ongoing works.
Cllr Slattery said the project had entered its seventh week and claimed sections of the town had been dug up without any visible activity for days at a time.

He questioned why contractors were not working Saturdays to complete the project during the peak tourism season. “The contractor is not coming in to finish that project within a timeframe that is acceptable,” he said.
Backing the concerns, Cllr Shane Talty (FF) said residents and businesses had been informed earlier that day (July 21) that the closure of Parliament Street would remain in place until August 28.

He said the extension meant the busiest weeks of the tourism season were now being affected, creating significant disruption for businesses, visitors and elderly people trying to access the town. Cllr Talty said many older people were now forced to park on the outskirts of Ennistymon before walking into the town centre.
“You can see them basically struggling to sustain themselves on those kind of walks in and out of the town,” he said.

He also questioned whether contractors delivering public projects were being held sufficiently accountable for delays, adding: “We need to be stronger on managing contractors to make good on the contracts that they are taking out.”

In response, Director of Services Carmel Kirby acknowledged the concerns and said the council would continue engaging with the project management team. She noted that sourcing specialist tradespeople could sometimes present difficulties and said similar issues had arisen during works in Ennis.

Acting Senior Engineer Paddy Tiernan said there has been no delay to the overall completion date of the project and said the extension of the Parliament Street closure was due to additional works requested by the ESB and the discovery of old culverts beneath the road.
Mr Tiernan said unforeseen issues were “unfortunately a risk” on projects involving old market towns and acknowledged the disruption the works were causing for local businesses.

“These public realm projects… it's hard to see the light when you're in the middle of them,” he said, adding that while the works were difficult in the short term, the completed project would ultimately benefit the town.
Cllr Slattery responded by questioning why underground issues had not been identified during earlier surveys, saying businesses were “losing a fortune” while the project continued.

Mr Tiernan replied that while most underground services are identified in advance, some culverts were likely more than 100 years old and had no records or maps, meaning they could only be discovered once excavation began.

title: O'Dea delivers for Bricks to win player of the week
excerpt: SHOWING no signs of rustiness, Caoilfhionn O’Dea led from the off to be named Martin Daly Autos/The Clare Echo player of the week.
author: Páraic McMahon
alt: O'Dea delivers for Bricks to win player of the week
body: SHOWING no signs of rustiness, Caoilfhionn O’Dea led from the off to be named Martin Daly Autos/The Clare Echo player of the week.
Kilmurry Ibrickane played some of the best football in round one of the Clare SFC as they defeated St Breckans 4-14 0-17.

To the fore for Enda Coughlan’s men was Caoilfhionn O’Dea at centre forward. He scored 2-1 with goals off either foot to the bottom and top corners of the net while he knitted the play together very well as Kilmurry Ibrickane tore the Spa defence apart on several occasions.

Making O’Dea’s display all the more impressive was it served as his first competitive outing since February. The Mullagh attacker hasn’t lined out properly since on as a substitute in the second round of the National Football League for Clare in February, he suffered a hamstring injury in the aftermath which sidelined him for over five months.

title: ‘Colossus of immense courage’: Clare GAA pays tribute to James McHugh
excerpt: CLARE GAA have paid tribute following the passing of former Donegal footballer James McHugh and his wife Noreen in a road traffic collision in Co. Cavan on Monday afternoon.
author: Michael Fitzgerald
alt: ‘Colossus of immense courage’: Clare GAA pays tribute to James McHugh
body: CLARE GAA have paid tribute following the passing of former Donegal footballer James McHugh and his wife Noreen in a road traffic collision in Co. Cavan on Monday afternoon.
Clare County Board acknowledged their sympathy in a post on social media which referenced his daughter Emma’s recent marriage to Scariff hurler Diarmuid Nash.

In their statement, Clare GAA highlighted that “The thoughts and deepest sympathies of everyone in Clare GAA are with Emma (McHugh) Nash, Diarmuid Nash, the McHugh family, their wide circle of friends, and all in Donegal and Kilcar GAA following the tragic passing of James and Noreen McHugh in a road traffic collision”.

McHugh’s talent and legacy as one of The Forgotten County’s greatest ever footballers was further referenced by Clare GAA who stated that “James will forever be remembered as one of Donegal’s greatest footballers – an All-Ireland winner and All Star with his brother Martin in 1992, a small man in stature but a colossus of immense courage, skill and humility on the field whose influence on Gaelic games reached far beyond his native county”.

The Chill Chartha clubman played for Donegal between 1990 and 1996 and usually lined out as a half-forward, winning two Ulster Senior Football titles and three Donegal club championships. A proud Gaeilgeoir, McHugh led his club to four Comórtas Peile na Gaeltachta titles between 1987 and 1991.
Brian McEniff, Donegal’s manager when they claimed their first All-Ireland in 1992 over Dublin, stated that he was “broken-hearted”, following the half-forward’s death.

“James was such a fine man. I had a great friendship with him. He is the first player from the 1992 panel we have lost – we had also lost selector Seamus Bonar. It is just terrible. I don’t know what to say. James had the heart of a lion. I can still remember him in Clones in the Ulster final nipping in before big Brian McGilligan and getting the ball”, he continued.
McHugh’s son Eoin and nephew Ryan are current members of the Donegal senior panel. Another nephew, Mark McHugh, managed Westmeath to a first Leinster title since 2004 this year.

An Garda Síochána are appealing for witnesses following the fatal road traffic collision which tragically claimed the couple’s lives on the N3 at Drummallaght, between Virginia and Cavan, Co Cavan, shortly before 2pm on Monday, August 10.

title: No injuries after Irish Red Cross minibus involved in Lissycasey crash
excerpt: A COLLISION involving an Irish Red Cross minibus and jeep saw all passengers involved escape without injury in Lissycasey.
author: Michael Fitzgerald
alt: No injuries after Irish Red Cross minibus involved in Lissycasey crash
body: A COLLISION involving an Irish Red Cross minibus and jeep saw all passengers involved escape without injury in Lissycasey.
The incident occurred on Monday at approximately 2pm at the townland of Gortygeeheen, just outside Lissycasey, on the N68 Ennis to Kilrush national route.

In a statement to The Clare Echo, a spokesperson for the Irish Red Cross explained that “[On Monday] afternoon an Irish Red Cross Community Support minibus was involved in a traffic incident in Co. Clare”.

“Thankfully all four passengers that were onboard at the time were not injured. They were transported to University Hospital Limerick for assessment, and all were discharged. Passengers in a second vehicle were also unharmed. We would like to thank the National Ambulance Service (NAS), the Fire Service and Gardaí for their response and support at the scene”, they continued.
The N68 was closed for a short time following the incident but reopened soon afterwards.

title: Down but not out – Doora/Barefield determined to bounce back in round two
excerpt: COUNTY FINALISTS last season, the 2026 campaign is already “different” for St Joseph’s Doora/Barefield who face a crunch tie with Kildysart this weekend.
author: Páraic McMahon
alt: Down but not out – Doora/Barefield determined to bounce back in round two
body: COUNTY FINALISTS last season, the 2026 campaign is already “different” for St Joseph’s Doora/Barefield who face a crunch tie with Kildysart this weekend.

An opening round draw last year between the sides would prove to be the only points they amassed in the group stages. Scoring difference sent Doora/Barefield through to the knockout stages with Kildysart ending up in a relegation battle.

Both roads led them on different paths, Kildysart successfully maintaining their status while Doora/Barefield took major scalps to eliminate Kilmurry Ibrickane and Cratloe before facing off with Éire Óg in their first Clare SFC final since 2012.
Injuries and availability has disrupted preparations for St Joseph’s Doora/Barefield. They remain without US based Darragh O’Shea, their captain of last year and James Curran (ACL).

Manager Donagh Vaughan outlined, “This year has been different for us and it has been more getting lads back on the field than having them there, it is what it is, we have to regroup and go for Kildysart”.

He added, “We’re still there, we’re getting lads back on the field, we are where we are, we have no real faults, we’re disappointed, we know we have a lot of work to do and a lot of improving for when we come up against Kildysart, we have to park it, dust ourselves down and look at what happened and what we can change, that is where we’re at”.
Beaten by five points to Ennistymon, The Parish were “disappointed but in all fairness in the second half Ennistymon got a grip on the game, that was ultimately the difference,” according to Vaughan.

One of the big disappointments from their defeat was their second half display where they only hit 1-2. “We started so well, we got a great lead, we got into our rhythm fairly quick but Ennistymon clawed their way back into the game. In the second half, we couldn’t really deal with Brendy (Rouine), he was everywhere, he was very effective for them, that was the big difference, we stayed at it and got a goal back, at the end of the day we can have no complaints and we have a lot of work to improve on certain areas”.

title: Two hospitalised after evening crash on Ennis relief road
excerpt: TWO people have been hospitalised following a traffic collision outside of Ennis on Tuesday evening.
author: Michael Fitzgerald
alt: Two hospitalised after evening crash on Ennis relief road
body: TWO people have been hospitalised following a traffic collision outside of Ennis on Tuesday evening.
The incident occurred at approximately 5.45pm on the N85 relief road on the approach to the M18 motorway, in westbound lanes between the Skehanagh and Clare Abbey roundabouts.
The scene was attended by Units of Clare County Fire and Rescue Service from Ennis station. As well as National Ambulance Service paramedics and Gardaí who attended the scene.

A lengthy traffic jam was caused by the collision as many people were using the busy commuter route at the time to return from work. The incident resulted in the left hard shoulder being blocked as a large bottleneck of traffic formed behind the site of the collision.

The passenger and driver from one of the cars involved were brought to hospital for treatment with non-serious injuries. The driver of the second vehicle in the crash was assessed at the scene by emergency services but was not brought to hospital.
The road was fully reopened at 7.15pm that evening.
